## Claims
- [source-backed] In the integral symmetric-function model, \(\Lambda=\Lambda_{\mathbb Z}\); the Schur functions are a \(\mathbb Z\)-basis, \(I_{r,n-r}\) is the \(\mathbb Z\)-span of shapes outside \((n-r)^r\), and \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\cong H^\ast(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\). [source-2, lines 1310-1330]
- [source-backed] The paper explicitly extends its type-\(A\) argument from characteristic-zero fields to the integral coinvariant algebra \(H^\ast(G/B,\mathbb Z)\). [source-2, lines 1339-1350]
- [source-backed] For \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\), with \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), the source states that \(J_v\) is generated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2, lines 1354-1375]
- [source-backed] Theorem 5.4 gives two smaller integral generating sets for \(J_v\) as an ideal of \(H^\ast(G/P_J,\mathbb Z)\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\), with \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\) and \(b=\min(i,j)\). [source-2, lines 1380-1402]
- [source-backed] The 2024 St. Dizier–Yong paper is identified by DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\); its supplied abstract says it proves the minimality conjecture, but supplies neither theorem text nor coefficient hypotheses concerning an integral Schur-span description of \(J_v\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832]
- [unsupported] The inspected records do not contain an exact external theorem statement asserting the stronger equality \(J_v=\bigoplus_{i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r}\mathbb Zs_\mu\), rather than the source’s integral *ideal-generation* statement. Thus this exact Schur-span identification remains ungrounded by a retrieved citable statement.

## Strategy
Use the integral model and ideal-generation statement from arXiv:0809.2981v2 only with coefficient ring \(\mathbb Z\). Do not substitute the metadata-only 2024 result for missing theorem text.

## Gaps
No inspected external full text supplies the requested exact integral Schur-span equality or its hypotheses. The DOI record is metadata/abstract only.

## Next
Retrieve and inspect a theorem/proposition from the full text of St. Dizier–Yong, DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\), or another primary source, that explicitly states the Schur-span equality and coefficient ring.
